topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture opens with learning outcomes and an overview of the hallmarks of cancer model.

topics.label: Growth signal independence and intracellular signaling cascades
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive autonomous cancer cell proliferation.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells fail to withdraw from the cell cycle and complete lineage differentiation in blood and intestinal tissues.

topics.label: Evading apoptosis, replicative senescence, and genome surveillance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how tumor cells bypass programmed cell death, telomere shortening, and p53-mediated stress responses to achieve limitless survival.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells alter metabolic pathways, shift toward aerobic glycolysis, and utilize oncometabolites to drive progression.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how growing tumors overcome diffusion limits by activating the angiogenic switch to recruit new blood vessels.

topics.label: Mechanisms, monitoring, and genetics of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the metastatic cascade, circulation tracking, tissue colonization barriers, and genomic features associated with metastatic spread.

topics.label: Summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture concludes with a review of cancer hallmarks, references to advanced literature, and final housekeeping for upcoming sessions.
